sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and router setup
sections.what: Loads the web tools, the shared settings object, and creates the router. Also states this file's purpose in a comment.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Changes made here affect the shared settings object used across the whole app.

sections.name: SettingsUpdate
sections.title: Request shape for changing settings
sections.what: Describes a change request in which every field is optional, so only one value needs to be sent.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the interface change one setting at a time.
sections.watch_out: Empty strings are skipped by the update logic, so a value cannot be cleared this way.

sections.name: SettingsResponse
sections.title: Reply shape for settings
sections.what: Describes what the settings read returns, including which AI models each provider uses.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: It must match what the read route returns, or the reply will fail the check.

sections.name: get_settings
sections.title: Reading current settings
sections.what: Returns the current settings and reports only whether an OpenAI key is set, never the key itself.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the secret key out of what the interface receives.
sections.watch_out: Adding the raw key to this reply would expose it to anyone who can reach the server.

sections.name: update_settings
sections.title: Changing settings
sections.what: Changes the provider, the OpenAI key and the OpenAI model names in memory. Rejects any provider other than ollama or openai.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the provider change without a restart. The docstring says persistent changes need environment variables.
sections.watch_out: There is no login or permission check, and the change affects the whole running app.

sections.name: get_available_providers
sections.title: Listing available providers
sections.what: Describes the two providers with their cost, privacy notes, requirements and model names.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The cost and privacy text is typed by hand, so it can fall out of date.

summary: Routes that read and change the app's AI provider and API key settings while it runs, and list the available providers.
purpose: Let the user switch between the free local AI service (Ollama) and paid OpenAI, and set an OpenAI key, from the interface.
why: Likely reason: lets the user change providers without editing files. The docstring notes the changes are not saved.
how: Reading returns the current settings without the key, only saying whether one is set. Updating changes the provider (only ollama or openai allowed), the key, and two OpenAI model names, in memory. The providers route returns descriptions and model names for both.
inputs: An update body with any of: provider, OpenAI key, OpenAI research model, OpenAI ingestion model.
outputs: Current settings, a confirmation message, or a bad-request error for an unknown provider.
risks: There is no login check, so anyone who can reach the server can change the provider and the key. Changes are lost on restart. The cost and privacy wording is fixed text.
debug: If the provider does not change, check the spelling in the request. After a restart, values return to the environment settings, so check the environment file for the saved defaults.
